text_content: davao the flood capital but perhaps not for the reason you think they say davao is the flood capital of the philippines well if someone insists on giving us that crown perhaps we should wear it proudly-but let's first ask a simple question what exactly is overflowing yes davao experiences floods we have rivers that swell after relentless rain low-lying communities that sometimes bear the brunt of nature sudden downpours that seem to arrive without an appointment and roads that occasionally transform into temporary swimming pools that is a real problem it deserves real solutions-not political theater but if we are going to compare cities perhaps the scoreboard deserves more than a political slogan during the severe southwest monsoon flooding in july 2025 for example the metropolitan manila development authority reported hundreds of flooding incidents across metro manila within a single day so before anyone points a finger at davao perhaps we should remember that flooding is not a problem exclusive to one city water does not check political affiliations before it rises rain does not ask who you voted for before it pours and rivers certainly don't read campaign speeches but here's where i see davao differently because there is another kind of flooding happening here-one that doesn't destroy homes close roads or leave mud behind davao floods with culture walk through this city and you encounter a living mosaic of mindanao indigenous traditions migrant communities different languages cuisines beliefs stories and histories woven together into one constantly evolving urban tapestry ask someone where they came from and you may discover an entire story behind the answer then inevitably there's food because in davao you can start a conversation about almost anything and somehow end up discussing durian this variety is sweeter no that one has better texture you haven't tried the best one yet suddenly what began as a casual conversation has transformed into an international conference on durian no registration fee required but perhaps davao's most remarkable flood is neither water nor culture it is warmth there is a quiet generosity in the character of many dabawenyos that statistics cannot measure you can arrive as a stranger and before long someone may already be telling you where to eat what places to visit which shortcut to take-and most importantly which road to avoid when traffic is terrible that's not just hospitality that's hospitality with a built-in traffic advisory and then there is davao's natural beauty the sea samal mount apo the forests the farms the rivers the mountains the wide spaces that remind you that progress and nature do not always have to be enemies davao is also changing businesses are arriving buildings are rising infrastructure is expanding communities are growing people continue to come-not only because they are looking for jobs but because they are looking for possibilities some arrive carrying résumés others arrive carrying business plans some arrive carrying nothing more than a dream and somewhere along the way many discover something unexpected they don't merely live in davao they become part of it that perhaps is the real story a city should not be judged solely by the problems that rise within it it should also be judged by what its people continue to build despite those problems davao is not perfect we have traffic we have growing pains we have environmental concerns we have infrastructure challenges we have political disagreements and of course we have social-media experts who can apparently repair the entire country using nothing but a smartphone and a facebook account but beneath all the noise is something far more difficult to construct character you can build a highway you can build skyscrapers you can build malls bridges offices and massive developments you can even build a spectacular roundabout that everyone will complain about for months but you cannot manufacture belonging you cannot pour it into concrete you cannot buy it from a catalog it has to grow and davao has grown through people people from different places came here they planted roots they built families they opened businesses they raised children they created communities and little by little their individual stories became part of the larger story of the city for the past 15 years i have had the privilege of traveling around davao for team-building activities retreats seminars workshops and speaking engagements and in those years i have seen something that no flood statistics can text_content: oo residente ako ng davao city kinuwestiyon ni dating philippine national police pnp chief nicolas torre iii ang patuloy na pagbaha sa davao city matapos muling bahain ang kanyang bahay sa nha bangkal barangay talomo kasunod ng malakas na ulan noong hulyo 24 sa kanyang social media post sinabi ni torre na nakapangalan sa kanya at sa kanyang asawa ang naturang bahay at bilang residente ng davao city ay may karapatan siyang magtanong kung bakit paulit-ulit pa ring nangyayari ang pagbaha ayon kay torre matagal nang alam na ang mga sanhi ng pagbaha tulad ng mountain runoff at malalakas na pag-ulan kaya dapat aniya ay may epektibong solusyon na lalo na't bilyon-bilyong piso na ang nagastos para sa mga flood control projects binigyang-diin niya na ang tunay na sukatan ng flood control ay hindi ang dami ng proyektong naipatupad kundi ang dami ng pamilyang hindi na naaabot ng baha naghahanap ako ng resulta hindi ng palusot saad ni torre lnb oo residente ako ng davao city
